body:
Could we replace the `.unwrap()` with an early return of `None`?
It would be best to simply not show the module than to panic.

yeah, `.unwrap()` was quite rude ;-)

How about the updated version (which is using `.unwrap_or_default()`)?
I also added a couple of additional tests:
- if the current working dir isn't recognized as an hg repo, the module shouldn't produce any output at all
- if it is an hg repo, but the module fails to retrieve a bookmark or branch name (e.g. because it fails to execute hg, not unlikely if it is not installed), it defaults to "(no branch)" (which let the user know that, even if an hg repo has been detected, something went wrong and so the branch name is missing)

How that sounds/looks to you?

yeah, you are right, I just had to turn an empty string output into None on the `get_hg_log_template` side  (because the '{activebookmark}' output could be an empty string and it would be good to fallback to the branch name in that case)

Thanks! This is so much nicer.

+

+| `truncation_symbol` | `"…"`           | The symbol used to indicate a branch name was truncated. You can use "" for no symbol        |

body:
I'm pretty sure that none that use mercurial would have to use that configuration option.

I have to confess that I added it mainly to be able to easily test that the module does fallback gracefully when all the mercurial commands fails to run successfully.

I was already unhappy (also a bit "guilty" :-)) about such an hacky testing strategy and so I took the opportunity to think to something else that would be less invasive (as it doesn't need to customize the hg binary name).

In the updated version the single test case that was using this config option is now using a fake "broken hg repo" (and I removed any trace of this unnecessary config option).
